findings.reason: §4 is the section a later node reads to learn when mapping runs, and its summary tells that node the default was kept, which is the exact reversal the decision recorded hours later.
findings.text: §4's landed summary says "The mapping domain runs by default in `imas-codex discover FACILITY`", while the `mapping-stage-default` decision in the same document (data-choice="opt-in", 2026-10-08T09:47:46) and §3's landed summary ("Mapping runs only as `--only mapping`") say the opposite; `sequence.py:615` returns "not requested" for mapping whenever `--only` is absent and `--until` gives no closure

findings.reason: §2's done-when bullet "each stage's `nothing to do` follows its named pending-work predicate" cannot hold as written, and the §7 nodes that edit these very modules are told the documents and wiki predicates are already in the registry when they are not.
findings.text: §2 (declared done) describes a nine-stage registry in which each stage's pending-work predicate is named by the registry, "the mapping stage records none" because "mapping is not a discover domain", and "the registry's documents stage calls only `has_pending_work`"; the built registry has eight stages (`_stage(` occurs 8 times in `imas_codex/cli/discover/sequence.py`), has no separate `signals check` stage (check folded into `signals enrich`'s pending tuple at :155-157), declares `pending=()` for both `documents` (:132) and `wiki` (:140) so neither named predicate group is wired, and records `domain="mapping"` for the mapping stage against `DOMAINS = (..., "mapping")` — `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` at `common.py:33` also contains `"map"`, so mapping is a discover domain

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: two findings — 10 of the 12 cited `file:line` anchors are stale by 4 to 270 lines and land in unrelated code, and both gate evidence `href` attributes carry prose instead of a target.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the §5 proof node's done-when names no negative control, so nothing shows that a stage which should have been skipped was reported as skipped.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate and fragment path is durable under `docs/evidence/fragments/facility-discovery-sequence/`, `docs/evidence/archive/` and `docs/figures/facility-discovery-sequence/`, and all of those resolve on disk.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the plan prescribes mechanism-named symbols (`resolve_focus_items`, `has_pending_work`) and no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag is prescribed into code; node ids such as `signal-status-monotonic` are tracker identifiers and stay in the plan, as they should.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — §4's landed summary states that mapping runs by default, which the plan's own later `mapping-stage-default` decision and §3 contradict; and §2's mechanism (nine stages, a names-predicate-per-stage registry, "mapping is not a discover domain") is not the mechanism in `imas_codex/cli/discover/sequence.py`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the implementable nodes each name one deliverable (one registry, one refusal rule, one focus filter per domain), and the §7 nodes not yet built are each described as one domain's filter with one named test file.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every cross-plan reference the plan names resolves in `docs/plans/jt60sa-discovery-completion.html` (`s56`, `jt60sa-jev-rescan`, `signal-status-monotonic`) and the two evidence gates carry `data-section`/`data-gated-sections`; section `data-links=""` is the house convention in this repo (62 of 62 in the sibling plan), so absence of link attributes is not a defect here.
